findings.title: Client-controlled query param bypasses intended pagination restrictions and permission check is insufficient
findings.body: The endpoint lets any authenticated user toggle `optimized_pagination=true` and relies on `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` to gate access. However, the `enable_advanced_features` path in OptimizedCursorPaginator allows arbitrary negative offsets supplied directly by the client cursor (`cursor.offset`), which is attacker-controlled input independent of this permission check. A user with global access (which is not necessarily a superuser, e.g. any org owner) can craft cursors with large negative offsets to access rows outside the normal paginated window, since the comment in paginator.py asserts "permissions are checked at the queryset level" but no actual queryset-level restriction is added — it's just a slice offset trick. This could allow reading unintended rows or causing unexpected DB query costs.

findings.title: Negative offset slicing produces invalid/undefined queryset behavior
findings.body: When `self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing/slicing (unlike Python lists) and will raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` at runtime. This means any client passing a negative-offset cursor to this paginator will cause a 500 error instead of being handled gracefully, contradicting the PR's claim of 'enhanced' pagination support.

findings.title: Incorrect result-trimming condition when negative offset is used
findings.body: The check `elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra` assumes `offset` is always non-negative (consistent with the original BasePaginator). When `enable_advanced_features` allows negative offsets, this arithmetic becomes incorrect, potentially leaving an extra row in `results` or stripping a valid row off the end, producing incorrect pagination boundaries/cursors even if the earlier negative-slice crash were fixed.

findings.title: No tests added for new OptimizedCursorPaginator
findings.body: The PR adds an entirely new paginator class (OptimizedCursorPaginator) with non-trivial new behavior (negative offset handling, enable_advanced_features flag) but includes no unit tests. Given the negative-offset slicing bug and altered trimming logic, this lack of test coverage means the regression would not be caught before release.

findings.title: Undocumented/experimental query parameter with no validation or documentation
findings.body: `optimized_pagination` is read directly from `request.GET` without being part of `AuditLogQueryParamSerializer`, so it's unvalidated and undocumented. There's no changelog, API doc update, or test added demonstrating the new behavior, making it hard for consumers or reviewers to know this flag exists and is intentional versus leftover debug/test code (the PR description just says "Test 1").
